data.title: Evonik Shares Tumble After BASF Ends Takeover Efforts
data.description:
By Sarah Sloat

Shares in Evonik tumbled after German chemicals company BASF said it dropped its efforts to acquire the company.

The stock fell 15% to 18.51 euros.

BASF said the decision followed Evonik's rejection of two offers.

"Despite the indication that BASF was prepared to consider a further moderate increase to its offer, the Executive Board of Evonik has not shown meaningful engagement until today," BASF said in a statement.

BASF also said that an assessment of Evonik's standalone prospects and risks didn't justify a higher valuation.

"Against this background, BASF does not consider it to be in the best interests of its shareholders to pursue the transaction at a higher price," BASF said.

Write to Sarah Sloat at sarah.sloat@wsj.com

data.title: Dollar takes a breather as investors eye Anthropic IPO
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dollar edges down, still near highest since April 2, 2025
  • Yen falls against dollar, euro as risk sentiment firms
  • Fed signals keep further rate hikes on investors' radar

By Saqib Iqbal Ahmed and Stefano Rebaudo

The dollar eased against most major peers on Thursday as its recent rally lost momentum ahead of AI company Anthropic's market debut, seen as a key test of appetite for riskier assets and broader market sentiment.

The dollar rally started on November 10 when hotter-than-expected US inflation data bolstered expectations that the US Federal Reserve would tighten its policy.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for a more aggressive response to inflation, while minutes of the central bank's October 27 to 28 meeting showed policymakers increasingly concerned that additional tightening might be needed.

"The dollar has had a good run here ... I think a lot of good news is priced into the dollar at this point," Shaun Osborne, chief ​currency strategist at Scotiabank, said.

"Dollar bulls are going to need more conviction or more bullish news to drive dollar gains in the short run here," said Osborne, who pegged some of the dollar's softer tone to a pickup in risk sentiment ahead of the Anthropic IPO.

Nasdaq futures rose on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO above the marketed range, bolstering expectations for a strong debut and reviving sentiment around AI stocks.

The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, when US President Donald Trump revealed a sweeping tariff package, triggering a selloff in US assets.

It was last down 0.2% at 103.65 , after reaching 103.97. The euro rose 0.2% to $1.1002.

Barclays analysts said fiscal stimulus and strong AI-related capital spending point to a resilient US economy, a wider output gap and higher-for-longer interest rates, all supportive of dollar strength.

The dollar's gains have come despite a selloff in technology shares.

A Deutsche Bank tracker following more than 100 foreign-domiciled exchange-traded funds showed large dip-buying of US stocks by foreigners over the last two weeks, the biggest buying spree so far this year. Such a move reinforces the view that the dollar has been supported by investor flows into US equities.

YEN SLIPS AS SAFE-HAVEN FLOWS FADE

The dollar was up 0.4% to 159.905 yen , snapping a four-day losing streak.

Analysts said that a further selloff in AI-linked assets could support the yen through safe-haven buying and repatriation flows, with the impact likely to be more pronounced against other currencies than against the dollar.

The risk-sensitive Aussie was about flat on the day after hitting a fresh 11-month low earlier in the session. Australia's employment fell for a second straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, bolstering the view that rates have likely peaked.

"The sharp hawkish repricing of Fed rate hike expectations is contributing (to) the weakness in commodity prices and related currencies," said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG.

UBS brought forward its forecast for the first Reserve Bank of Australia rate cut to August next year from November, and extended the easing cycle to three cuts from two, citing elevated inflation and a deterioration in the labour and housing markets.

Sterling pulled back from a 20-month high against the euro, though investors remained upbeat about the UK interest rate outlook and wary of headwinds facing the single currency ahead of key elections across Europe in 2027. The pound rose 0.1% against the dollar to $1.3162.

In cryptocurrency markets, bitcoin rose 2.5% to $63,870, pulling away from the four-month low of $62,026 touched on Sunday, aided by stronger risk appetite.

data.title: Rand near one-year low as South African central bank holds rates
data.description:
The rand held near its weakest level this year against the dollar after the South African Reserve Bank kept its main interest rate unchanged on Thursday, with its governor saying monetary policy was tight enough after two hikes in 2026.

  • At 1420 GMT, the rand traded at 17.3050 against the dollar , little moved from its previous close and near the year’s low of 17.36

  • The risk-sensitive currency has recently been pressured by a firmer greenback, softer precious-metal prices and uncertainty around local government coalition talks

  • The rand fell about 2.3% last week and is on course to shed more than 2% this week

  • Thursday’s decision was a close call, with four Monetary Policy Committee members voting for no change in the policy rate and three favouring a 25-basis-point increase

  • Johann Els, chief economist at PSG, said: "The overall tone of the (MPC) statement was relatively balanced, despite the slightly hawkish signal from the vote"

  • Domestic investor attention remains on coalition talks, as local government elections have raised questions about the stability of South Africa's Government of National Unity as the African National Congress and the pro-business Democratic Alliance work to finalise local power-sharing agreements

  • The ANC and smaller rivals are closing in on a deal to govern Johannesburg, the country's economic hub, sidelining the DA despite its first-place finish in the city

  • On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index was last down 0.4%, while South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) strengthened, with the yield falling 7 basis points to 8.64%

data.title: PermRock Royalty Trust Declares $103,165 Monthly Distribution
data.description:
PermRock Royalty Trust declared a monthly cash distribution of $103,164.56, or $0.008479 per unit, payable December 14, 2026, to unitholders of record November 30. The distribution is based principally on September production and reflects the first installment of a prior overpayment recoupment. Oil receipts increased from the prior distribution period, primarily because of higher oil prices.

Financial Highlights

  • The declared distribution totals $103,164.56, or $0.008479 per trust unit.
  • Oil cash receipts were $1.18 million, up $0.17 million from the prior distribution period.
  • Natural gas cash receipts were $0.05 million, up approximately $0.01 million; other revenue was $0.01 million.
  • Direct operating expenses were $0.54 million, up approximately $0.08 million. Severance and ad valorem taxes were $0.06 million, up approximately $0.01 million.
  • The net profits calculation included a $165,000 net holdback and a $58,469 reduction to the Trust from the first installment of the $350,812.13 overpayment recoupment.

Business Highlights

  • Underlying oil sales were 12,761 barrels, averaging 425 barrels per day; natural gas sales were 15,934 Mcf, averaging 531 Mcf per day.
  • Average received wellhead prices were $92.63 per barrel of oil and $2.93 per Mcf of natural gas. The Trust attributed higher oil receipts mainly to increased oil prices and higher natural gas receipts mainly to increased gas prices, partly offset by lower gas volumes.
  • Capital expenditures totaled $41,794, primarily for tangible drilling and completion costs.
  • The Trust’s net profits interest entitles it to 80% of net profits from oil and natural gas production on certain Permian Basin properties operated by T2S.

data.title: BASF says it ends pursuit of Evonik after rejection of $12 billion bid
data.description:
BASF said on Thursday it would no longer try to acquire Evonik , following Evonik's rejection of two all-cash proposals.

"The Executive Board of Evonik has not shown meaningful engagement until today," even though BASF had indicated it was considering a further "moderate increase" of its offer, the German chemical giant said in a statement.

BASF first approached Evonik in September, but Evonik had resisted the advances and recently rejected ⁠a sweetened offer that valued the company at around €11.2 billion ($12.3 billion), or €24 per share.

On Tuesday, people familiar with the matter told Reuters that BASF was preparing to offer greater concessions to Evonik.

As part of its overtures, BASF had approached the local government in Evonik's home state of North Rhine-Westphalia and its top shareholder, the RAG Foundation, with a letter offering possible commitments to plants, jobs and training, the sources said.

Evonik shares plunged 17% at 1420 GMT, while BASF shares gained 1.2%.

Evonik did not have an immediate comment.
